standard_prerequisites.use: The chapter's lemma quasi-finite-quasi-section-meeting-nearby-open-X (the source of the conclusions; queued as the next wave's card for the X-version), Noetherianity of finite type schemes over locally Noetherian bases, quasi-compactness of opens in Noetherian spaces, and the scheme-theoretic-image specialization fact.

core_obligations: Shrink to affine Noetherian neighbourhoods of the two points.
Produce the specialization point x' in U via scheme-theoretic images.
Check f(x') != s so the cited lemma applies verbatim.

proof_roadmap.step: Affine-local Noetherian reduction and quasi-compactness of U.

difficulty_reason: The lemma swaps the hypotheses of the chapter's quasi-section lemma (lemma-quasi-finite-quasi-section-meeting-nearby-open-X) for weaker-looking but equivalent-for-the-purpose ones: f : X -> S locally of finite type with S locally Noetherian, x a closed point of its fibre X_s, U an open missing the fibre through x with x in the closure of U; then the conclusions of the cited quasi-finite lemma hold. The retained proof is a written reduction: shrink X and S to affine neighbourhoods of x and s, so X is Noetherian (cited Morphisms lemma finite-type-noetherian and the two Topology lemmas that Noetherian spaces are quasi-compact), hence U is quasi-compact, and the scheme-theoretic-image lemma (Morphisms, lemma reach-points-scheme-theoretic-image) supplies a specialization x' -> x with x' in U; the image point of x' differs from s, so the original quasi-finite-lemma hypotheses at (x', f(x')) are met and the reduction is justified line by line. Retained author proof at lines 15063-15075.

dedup.scope: Hypothesis variant of the nearby-open quasi-section lemma with explicit written reduction.
